items.title: BSE to replace Wipro in Nifty 50 index
items.description: In a notable change effective September 30, BSE shares will enter the Nifty 50 index, taking over Wipro's longstanding position since January 2002. This decision comes on the heels of BSE's impressive growth this year, while Wipro's market performance has waned. The adjustments by NSE aim to enhance broader representation across the market indices.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Opening the week on a cautious note, domestic equities saw the Nifty making slight gains, bolstered by targeted stock purchases as Q1 earnings unfold. This week is expected to carry a positive market trajectory, propelled by earnings trends and sector performance. Investors will keep a keen eye on the durability of earnings recovery and global happenings, particularly the US-Iran dialogues.

items.title: Stocks in news: Wipro, BSE, Vodafone Idea, Hyundai India and Airtel
items.description: The markets experienced fluctuations as they weighed the prospects of interest rates against concerns over oil prices and geopolitical issues. In notable changes, Wipro will exit the Nifty index, making way for BSE Ltd's entry. Vodafone Idea reported a reduction in first-quarter losses, while Bharti Airtel formed a partnership to enhance digital offerings.

items.title: Brokerages raise SBI target price after Q1 earnings beat
items.description: State Bank of India shares faced a 2.2 percent decline on Monday, despite surpassing analysts' expectations for their June-quarter earnings. Most brokerages expressed continued optimism for the lender, with several firms increasing their target prices while maintaining a positive outlook. The consensus 12-month target price indicates a considerable potential upside from Monday's closing figures.

items.title: Indian equities could hit new highs next year: Aditya Birla MF
items.description: Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund is optimistic about Indian equities potentially hitting new peaks shortly. This positive outlook is bolstered by robust earnings growth and a stable rupee which are likely to propel market gains. Taking into account the current elevated valuations, a methodical approach to stock selection is vital.

items.title: India is scanning more and withdrawing less as digital payments take over
items.description: India’s payments network is shifting towards software-based channels, with UPI QR codes and online card transactions growing while ATMs and other hardware-based infrastructure stagnate or decline. UPI QR codes rose 16.9% year-on-year to 792.6 million in June.

items.title: NBFCs outpace banks in June as cards lose some credit
items.description: NBFCs outpaced banks in retail lending growth in June, with loans rising over 20% year-on-year compared with 16% for banks. Growth was driven by jewellery and consumer durable loans as banks remained cautious in unsecured and low-ticket lending segments.

items.title: HDFC Bank cuts MCLR by 5 bps, Bank of Baroda raises 3-month rate by 10 bps
items.description: HDFC Bank reduced its lending rates by five basis points across maturities. Bank of Baroda will increase its three-month lending rate by ten basis points. HDFC's new rates became effective from August seventh for various tenors. Bank of Baroda's revised rate will take effect from August twelfth. The banks are adjusting their marginal cost of funds based lending rates.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: Indian Metal & Ferro Alloys, SBI among 5 stocks that could give 10-30% return
items.description: Brokerages are betting on a fresh leg of upside in select metal, banking and cement stocks, with five stocks emerging as key BUY calls.We have collated a list of recommendations from top brokerage firms from ETNow and other sources:

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 9 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, nine stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on August 10, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. Traders use the 200-day daily moving average (DMA) as a key indicator to determine the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: Rupee falls 11 paise on firm dollar, costlier crude
items.description: The Indian rupee weakened by 11 paise against the US dollar, closing at ₹95.28. A firming dollar, driven by rising global crude oil prices and ongoing West Asia tensions, pressured the rupee. While RBI intervention offered some support, the market remains watchful of geopolitical uncertainties impacting currency movements.

items.title: Bharat Forge among 4 F&O stocks with sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of August 10, four stocks in the NSE F&O pack recorded a sharp rise in futures open interest, with open interest increasing by more than 10% compared with the previous trading session. Futures open interest represents the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a particular security. A rise in open interest indicates that market participants are either initiating new positions or increasing their existing positions in the futures market.

items.title: Vodafone Idea shares jump 3% after Q1 net loss narrows. What is Nomura saying?
items.description: Vodafone Idea’s Q1 loss narrowed sharply to Rs 3,754 crore from Rs 6,608 crore a year ago, while revenue rose 6% YoY to Rs 11,689 crore. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs 5,034 crore, with margin improving to 43.1%, while ARPU jumped 10.2% to Rs 195.

items.title: Sensex falls over 300 points, Nifty below 24,550 as oil prices rise. What lies ahead?
items.description: On Tuesday, Indian stock markets experienced a downturn influenced by increasing oil prices and escalating tensions in the Middle East. Nevertheless, the broader markets displayed resilience as small and midcap indices thrived. Foreign institutional investors found encouragement in favorable Q1 outcomes and a stable rupee, suggesting that the market could maintain its strength with a slight upward trend. Strong domestic consumption is projected to support earnings growth through FY27.

items.title: Jubilant Pharmova among 4 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On August 10, four stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Aegeus Technologies shares to debut today: GMP signals 11% premium ahead of BSE SME listing
items.description: Aegeus Technologies is set to debut on the BSE SME platform after its Rs 23.71 crore IPO was subscribed nearly 30 times. The latest grey market premium of Rs 12 implies a potential listing price of Rs 117. The robotics and automation company reported 88% revenue growth and 189% profit growth in FY26.

items.title: Avenue Supermarts among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On August 10, four Nifty500 stocks that rallied over 3% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from stockedge.com. It is an uptrend signal if the RSI value has crossed above 50 from below. "RSI trending up" means that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, suggesting strengthening momentum in the price of the stock. This can indicate potential upward movement and may be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: Adani Group stocks jump up to 3% after US judge drops criminal case against Gautam Adani. What investors should know
items.description: Adani Group shares rose up to 3% after a US judge dismissed criminal charges against Gautam Adani. Adani Enterprises, Adani Power, Adani Ports and Adani Green gained, boosting investor sentiment. The judge said the decision was not an endorsement of the Justice Department’s move, while Adani Group has consistently denied wrongdoing.

items.title: PC Jeweller share price jumps 6% as Q1FY27 profit surges 37% YoY, revenue up 21%
items.description: PC Jeweller shares rose sharply after Q1FY27 profit jumped 37% year-on-year and revenue grew 21%. The jewellery retailer also reported a sharp improvement in operating profitability, continued progress on debt repayment and increased FII holding. With plans to become debt-free and raise up to Rs 1,000 crore via QIP, key triggers remain.

items.title: 4 Vedanta Group stocks to see inflows worth $160 million in Nifty September rejig. What investors must know
items.description: Four newly demerged Vedanta entities could attract combined passive inflows of up to $159 million following the NSE Indices’ September 2026 reshuffle, according to Nuvama Alternative and Quantitative Research. Vedanta Aluminium Metal is expected to receive the bulk of the inflows, while Vedanta Power and Vedanta Iron and Steel could each see around $3 million.

items.title: Infosys, Vedanta among 10 stocks that saw the sharpest decrease in LIC holdings in Q1. See full list
items.description: Life Insurance Corporation of India’s portfolio moves are once again in focus. The insurance giant trimmed its holdings in several listed companies during the latest quarter, offering investors a closer look at how the country’s largest domestic institutional investor is repositioning its bets amid volatile markets and shifting sector trends.

items.title: Info Edge shares jump 4% after strong Q1 show. What Nomura, Nuvama and other brokerages expect next
items.description: Info Edge shares jumped over 4% after the company reported a strong Q1 FY27 performance, with consolidated net profit rising 43% year-on-year to Rs 490 crore. Recruitment billings grew 17.5%, while operating profit rose 25%. Nomura, Nuvama and Motilal Oswal retained their respective ratings, with Nomura and Nuvama maintaining Buy calls and raising target prices.

items.title: Nifty price-to-book valuation hits pre-Covid level. Why the index is still not cheap
items.description: Nifty's price-to-book ratio has dipped below three for the first time in years, highlighting a significant shift. Despite this, earnings remain at high valuations, suggesting minimal potential for multiple expansions. Future advancement in the market will depend more on profit enhancements instead of valuation adjustments. India's economic outlook looks promising, with several firms outperforming expectations, necessitating careful stock and sector choices to achieve alpha.

items.title: Gland Pharma shares rally 12% after Q1FY27 profit jumps 47% YoY. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: Gland Pharma shares rose sharply after Q1FY27 profit rose 47% and revenue grew 20% year-on-year. While strong margins and CDMO growth prompted Elara Securities to raise its earnings estimates, the brokerage downgraded the stock to ‘Accumulate’ from ‘Buy’ after its 40% three-month rally, citing limited near-term upside.

items.title: Paytm shares recover 410% from 2024 low, but will long-awaiting IPO investors finally see redemption?
items.description: Paytm shares have soared over 410 percent from their lowest levels, igniting hopes among investors that the stock will soon hit its initial public offering price. Bernstein's increased target price offers a promising outlook, suggesting a strong uptrend following a period of consolidation. The future of this recovery will hinge on key support levels as the market evolves.

items.title: Eternal vs Swiggy: The quick commerce war is on. Which stock should you own after Q1?
items.description: The rivalry in the quick commerce sector heats up as Q1 results show stark contrasts between Eternal and Swiggy. While Swiggy leans towards aggressive growth supported by robust funding, Eternal places its bets on profitability and improved operations. Both firms are vying for ambitious long-term goals that investors will be keen on observing, particularly in how they each navigate the balance between expansion and profitability.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Morgan Stanley remains overweight on Bharat Forge; Mirae Asset Sharekhan recommends buy on DEE Development Engineers
items.description: Brokerages remain positive on select stocks following Q1 FY27 earnings, with Morgan Stanley retaining an Overweight rating on Bharat Forge and raising its target, while Goldman Sachs maintained a Buy on Info Edge. Mirae Asset Sharekhan also retained a Positive view on DEE Development Engineers, citing strong order inflows, a healthy order book and robust growth prospects.

items.title: BSE shares to join rival NSE's benchmark index Nifty 50. What this means for shareholders
items.description: BSE will replace Wipro in the Nifty 50 from September 30, with Nuvama estimating $695 million inflows into BSE and $240 million outflows from Wipro. BSE shares are up 37% in 2026 despite a 6% monthly decline.

items.title: Retail investors make Rs 18,000 crore bold contra bet on 6 falling bluechip stocks. Will it pay off?
items.description: In a bold move, retail investors invested a whopping Rs 18,000 crore in six blue-chip stocks that were on a downward trend. They scooped up shares of Infosys, Reliance Industries, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, and ITC during the June quarter. While retail players flocked to these tech stocks, institutional investors were offloading their shares.

items.title: Global Market: Mainland Chinese stocks mixed, Hong Kong shares slip as Iran conflict weighs on sentiment
items.description: Chinese stocks traded mixed and Hong Kong shares edged lower as investors weighed fading hopes of a US-Iran peace deal and its impact on oil prices. Crude stayed near one-week highs amid Strait of Hormuz disruptions, fuelling concerns over global supplies and inflation.

items.title: Oil India shares jump over 5%. What made Emkay upgrade the stock after Q1 results
items.description: Oil India shares jumped over 5% after strong Q1FY27 results prompted Emkay Global to upgrade the stock to ‘Buy’. The brokerage cited attractive valuations, higher crude production and improving gas evacuation prospects. Elara Capital also retained its ‘Buy’ rating, while Nomura and Motilal Oswal maintained neutral views on the stock.

items.title: Jubilant Pharmova shares decline 6% after Q1 profits falls 45% YoY
items.description: Jubilant Pharmova shares fell after Q1 profit plunged 45% YoY to Rs 56 crore, despite revenue rising 17% to Rs 2,229 crore. The profit decline was attributed to weaker operating profitability and higher depreciation, while strong growth across segments, led by CDMO Sterile Injectables, boosted revenue.

items.title: Jupiter Wagons shares rise 4% after Rs 211 crore order wins, Rs 400 crore BESS project
items.description: Jupiter Wagons marked a notable surge in share prices due to securing significant contracts for freight wagons and energy storage solutions. With orders exceeding Rs 211 crore from the JSW Group and OASPL, alongside two battery energy storage initiatives worth Rs 400 crore, the company aims to bolster its market share in India, targeting a Rs 1,000 crore BESS order book by FY27.

items.title: Aarti Pharmalabs shares rally over 33% in two days post Q1 results. What is driving the surge?
items.description: Aarti Pharmalabs shares have surged 33% in two days after the company reported a 65.4% year-on-year rise in Q1FY27 profit and 38.7% growth in revenue. The rally was further supported by a Rs 149-crore capex plan to add 405 KL of capacity for its CDMO and intermediate businesses.

items.title: Without Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway is no longer an attractive investment: ‘Big Short’ fame Michael Burry
items.description: Veteran investor Michael Burry said Berkshire Hathaway has lost its investment appeal after Warren Buffett’s succession, arguing that Greg Abel may lack Buffett’s patience for major opportunities. Burry also flagged concerns over Berkshire’s large cash pile, saying its recent moves appear more strategic than investment-focused.

items.title: ideaForge Technology shares slide 5% after Q1 gross profit margin falls 49%
items.description: ideaForge Technology shares fell after its Q1 gross profit margin declined to 49% from 62% a year ago and 68% in the previous quarter. Gross profit rose to Rs 33.6 crore and revenue increased to Rs 68.6 crore, while EBITDA turned positive at Rs 4.3 crore.

items.title: Lumax Auto Technologies shares rally 19% after Q1 earnings
items.description: Lumax Auto Technologies shares surged after Q1 profit jumped 83% YoY to Rs 99 crore, while revenue grew 33% to Rs 1,364 crore. EBITDA rose 51% to Rs 205 crore, with margins expanding 190 bps to 15.1% on operational efficiencies, cost optimisation and a favourable product mix.

items.title: Intel’s $15 billion stock sale. Why shares fell despite AI boom
items.description: Intel has launched a plan to raise $15 billion through a new common-stock offering as the chipmaker looks to strengthen its finances and fund its expansion in AI and semiconductor manufacturing.

items.title: KPI Green Energy shares fall 6% after Q1 results. What's worrying investors?
items.description: KPI Green Energy shares fell sharply on Tuesday after the company reported a 14% year-on-year decline in Q1 net profit to Rs 94.63 crore. Rising finance costs and depreciation expenses weighed on profitability despite 16% revenue growth. Investors are also watching the company’s debt levels and cash flow as capacity expands.

items.title: How Wipro's Nifty exit shows old warhorse Indian IT is losing charm
items.description: Wipro’s exit from the Nifty 50 and BSE’s inclusion highlight the shifting composition of India’s benchmark index. The move comes as IT stocks face concerns over AI disruption and weakening investor interest. Wipro shares are down sharply in 2026, while the combined Nifty 50 weight of India’s top IT companies has fallen.

items.title: Mid-cap stocks: Time for a change of stance? 6 mid-caps from different sectors with an upside potential up to 29%
items.description: Sometimes the real market story is not in the headline index. The Nifty and Sensex can be under pressure, and yet, below them, mid- and small-cap stocks may be doing better. That is happening now, and there are reasons behind it that are worth understanding. But here’s the thing to remember: Mid-caps reward patience and punish haste. So the question is not whether to buy them, but for how long.

items.title: Axis Direct highlights 3 stocks showing bullish momentum for August. Do you own any?
items.description: The following three stocks are showing strong technical setups, with decisive breakouts, improving momentum and bullish trend structures, according to a monthly report by Axis Direct. Based on their price action and technical indicators, the brokerage sees further upside potential, with defined buying ranges, stop-loss levels and targets for traders to track.

items.title: MFs pull back: Stakes cut in 12 smallcap stocks after two quarters of buying; stocks fall up to 40%
items.description: An analysis of mutual fund (MF) shareholding trends in BSE smallcap stocks over the last four quarters reveals a notable shift. During the June 2026 quarter, mutual funds trimmed their holdings in 83 stocks, marking a reversal after two consecutive quarters of accumulation i.e. from September 2025 to December 2025, and again from December 2025 to March 2026.Of these stocks, 41 have delivered positive price returns in CY26 so far. In fact, 13 stocks have seen their share prices rise more than 50%, including two multibaggers. However, not all stocks have shared this upside. We identified 12 stocks from the group whose shares have declined by 20-40% during CY26, underlining the growing divergence in performance within the broader market.Mutual funds are considered by informed investors who often base their investment decisions on in-depth research and long-term fundamentals. While mutual fund buying typically boosts investor confidence, a reduction in their stakes after a period of steady accumulation is worth paying attention to. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Don't worry about AI! Why PPFAS CIO Rajeev Thakkar wants Indian investors to read what tech analyst Benedict Evans said
items.description: PPFAS CIO Rajeev Thakkar says fears that AI will destroy IT jobs are exaggerated. Citing Benedict Evans and historical automation, he argues technology eliminates some roles while creating new work, with implementation, cybersecurity and other opportunities emerging.

items.title: Can SIFs bridge the gap between mutual funds and alternative investments?
items.description: Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs) introduced a new investment framework for experienced investors. As portfolios evolve beyond traditional asset classes, could SIFs become the missing link between mutual funds and alternative investments?
